title: Quickstart Zen Paths for Embedded Clients (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a minimal, low-friction set of quickstart 'paths' for embedded client integrations (web/mobile/backend) that prioritize first-success, observability, and predictable cost. Goal: give a small team everything they need to ship a safe, instrumented integration in three friction tiers (10-min demo -> 1-day guided -> 1-week production hardening).

Why 'Zen' paths?
- Reduce decision points: each path has opinionated defaults (model, timeout, batching)
- Make success metrics explicit (first-success-rate, error-signal, cost-per-10k-requests)
- Provide a single-truth checklist for engineering, docs, and solutions engineers

Audience:
- Integrators: devs embedding Redwood API in product flows
- Solutions engineers: quick triage and handoff artifacts
- DX writers: convert checklist into a one-page quickstart and code samples

Summary of the three paths:
1) Hello-Minute: 10-minute 'smoke to demo' for a single endpoint (text generation).
2) Guided Integration: 1-day polish with retry/fallback, minimal telemetry, local dev tips.
3) Production Ready: 1-week checklist for SLA, rate limiting, batching, prompt evals, and cost tuning.

1) Hello-Minute path (10–15 min)
- Objective: Developer gets a streaming response in a sample app with a prebuilt prompt.
- Opinionated defaults: model=redwood-standard-1, timeout=4s, streaming=true, no retries, max_tokens=256
- Steps:
  - Prereqs: API key (free credit), quick page template (html + minimal JS), network allowed to api.redwood.ai
  - Copy sample snippet: (JS fetch simplified)
    fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $API_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-standard-1', prompt: 'Summarize: ...', stream: true })
    })
  - Show streaming output in a text area (append chunks)
  - Success criteria: first streaming token displayed within 600ms for local dev and non-empty result returned
- UX tips: Clear error copy for 401/429; show 'retry' button (manual)
- Telemetry to enable (minimal): quickstart_first_success boolean, demo_latency_ms metric, demo_error_code label

2) Guided Integration (1 day)
- Objective: Integrate a core use-case in non-production, with simple failover and telemetry.
- Opinionated defaults: model=redwood-high-accuracy-1 (or quantized variant for cost), timeout=8s, retry_policy=1x linear backoff, batching disabled by default
- Step checklist:
  - Scaffold client wrapper (language-specific) with automatic auth header handling and env var support
  - Implement safe prompt framing helper (escape user input / content filter preflight)
  - Add client-side retry for transient 5xx/429 with exponential backoff capped at 2s
  - Add fallback path: when API fails, route to simple deterministic stub response or local template to preserve UX
  - Add telemetry hooks: request_id, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_class
  - Smoke tests: run 25 requests with realistic prompts, assert <5% error rate and median latency <1.5x benchmark
- Dev ergonomics: provide docker-compose for a local proxy that simulates rate-limited errors and consistent latency for testing
- Docs to ship together: short README + troubleshooting FAQ + one confluence page linking to relevant PRs

3) Production Ready (1 week)
- Objective: Harden the integration for SLA, cost, observability, and maintainability
- Opinionated defaults & policies:
  - Pin model versions (do not use floating alias in prod routes)
  - Use batching for high-throughput routes; configure batching windows and max batch size per route
  - Enable KV/prefix caching for common, repeated prompts if applicable
  - Configure circuit-breaker: open after N consecutive failures, degrade to cheaper model variant rather than full outage
  - Quota & rate limit config per client (tie to org/account)
- Implementation checklist:
  - Create route-level instrumentation: token_cost_per_request, route_p95_latency, tail_error_rate
  - Configure rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regression (evaluate against prompt-suite)
  - Add e2e prompt evaluation harness: golden set + acceptance thresholds (semantic similarity >= 0.78 or BLEU >= X depending on task)
  - Cost tuning: evaluate CPU/GPU-backed model variants and quantized variants on representative workload to estimate cost delta; set default variant per route
  - SRE items: alert on sustained token-price spikes, increased p99 latency, or increased inference error class rate
  - Data controls: if sensitive data flows, enable request-level audit logging to the customer's private sink or redact at SDK layer

Production safety & compliance notes:
- Provide example KMS integration snippet and advice for not storing raw user text unencrypted in logs
- Recommend privacy-preserving trimming in SDK helper: keep only last N tokens, drop ephemeral user metadata, hash IDs before logging

Telemetry & KPIs (what to measure ASAP)
- Setup (minimum): first_success_rate (per-route), median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens/1000_requests (cost proxy), fallback_rate, prompt-regression-alerts
- Dashboards: one route-level quickstart dashboard (first_success_rate, cost proxy, p95) and one account-level health dashboard (saturation, top error classes)

Release artifacts to produce
- One-page quickstart (public docs) distilled from this doc (Hello-Minute + code snippet + 3 troubleshooting bullets)
- Developer sample repo with three folders matching the three paths (hello, guided, prod-harden) and a small test harness that can replay prompt-sets
- Solutions engineer playbook (2 pages) that includes escalation steps, common tickets, and recommended A/B policies

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Q1: Should Hello-Minute sample default to streaming or non-streaming? (Pros: streaming feels fast; Cons: adds complexity on mobile web) -> lean streaming for demo, non-streaming for mobile sample
- Q2: Canonical model names for examples (need PM alignment) -> create alias mapping ticket JIRA-7890
- Q3: Local proxy test harness: provide a small Python service that simulates throttling and injects 500/503s. Samir to prototype
- TODO: Pair with docs writer to convert the Hello-Minute into a one-page Quickstart with screenshots (owner: Priya)

Appendix: Sample Lightweight JS wrapper (pseudo)
- purpose: show minimal wrapper that centralizes retry, telemetry hook, and safe prompt helper
- pseudo: 
function redwoodClient(apiKey) {
  return {
    async generate(params) {
      const start = Date.now();
      // call fetch, retry once on 5xx/429, attach request-id and emit telemetry hooks
      // return parsed text stream or full text depending on params.stream
    }
  }
}

Notes about docs style:
- Keep examples as short as possible (<=30 lines)
- Use progressive disclosure: a single-file hello-world, then a guided folder with helpers, then a production examples folder with CI and e2e scripts

Landing plan for rollout:
- Week 0: merge sample repo + quick internal confluence page -> invite 4 SEs to validate
- Week 1: iterate examples based on SE feedback and add mobile-specific guidance
- Week 2: publish public quickstart and link from main SDK README; track first_success_rate for the quickstart route

Contacts: Elena Martinez (owner), Marcus Li (sample repo), Priya Reddy (docs), Samir Khan (test harness)

-- End of draft --
